turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hello, I’m 35, and for about a month I’ve had double vision that’s worse when I’m active. I also feel weakness when climbing stairs and when I try to brush my hair, but it improves a lot after I rest for a few hours.”

turns.doctor_question: I'm sorry to hear you're not feeling well. To help me better understand what you're experiencing, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as blurriness, dark spots, or any loss of sight?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, it’s more like true double vision—objects look split—rather than blurry vision. I haven’t noticed dark spots or any loss of sight, just the doubling that gets worse with activity and then eases after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: To help me get a better picture of your overall health, could you tell me if you currently smoke or have a history of smoking?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t smoke and I’ve never smoked.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of how you're feeling, have you been experiencing any nausea or feeling sick to your stomach lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had nausea or any stomach upset. I feel mostly the vision doubling and the muscle weakness, which both seem to flare with activity and then improve after a few hours of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your health, have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breast area that do not cause you any pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breast area, and I don’t have any pain or tenderness there.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand that physical symptoms can sometimes be linked to how we are feeling emotionally. To help me get a clearer picture of your overall well-being, have you been experiencing a significant amount of psychological stress lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not particularly—no major psychological stress, and nothing else feels emotionally out of the ordinary. It seems much more tied to activity: the symptoms worsen with exertion and then improve after I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: To help me better understand your current symptoms, have you noticed any changes in the color of your urine, specifically if it has appeared darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any change in the color of my urine—it's been normal and not darker than usual.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand that finding a change in your breast can be concerning. To help me better understand what you are experiencing, could you tell me if you have noticed this mass growing or changing in size rapidly over a short period of time?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or breast changes at all, so nothing is growing or changing rapidly.”

turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any wrist pain. My main issues have been the double vision and the weakness with things like climbing stairs or brushing my hair, which improve after rest.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your health, I’d like to ask about your breathing: Do you find that you experience shortness of breath or difficulty catching your breath when you are physically active, such as walking or climbing stairs?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t get shortness of breath or have trouble catching my breath. It’s mainly the double vision and the weakness—those flare with activity, and then I improve after resting for a few hours.”

turns.doctor_question: To help me get a clearer picture of your health, could you tell me if you have used any recreational or non-prescribed drugs recently?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t used any recreational or non-prescribed drugs recently. I haven’t taken anything besides occasional wine socially.”
